newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire government denounces aid deal with rebels.
newsitem.headline: Zaire government denounces aid deal with rebels.

text.p: Zaire's government on Monday denounced a deal between aid groups and Tutsi rebels to channel aid to refugees in the east of the country as a violation of its territorial integrity.

Government spokesman and Information Minister Boguo Makele told Reuters that Zaire had no objection to aid arriving in the Central African country via the capital Kinshasa and being distributed to displaced Zaireans.
But he denounced aid taken into the rebel-held refugee town of Goma from Rwanda on Monday by the U.N. and independent aid groups
"This constitutes a violation of our territorial integrity," he said. "Aid for the (Rwanda) refugees should be distributed in Rwanda."
Over a million Hutus fled from Rwanda to Zaire in fear of reprisals in 1994 after Hutu hardliners massacred hundreds of thousands of minority Tutsis and their sympathisers.
Boguo said Zaire had agreed to creation of a multinational military intervention force to set up a corridor to enable the refugees to return from Zaire to Rwanda.

Zairean Tutsi rebels launched an offensive near the border with Burundi more than three weeks ago. They hold most major towns in North and South Kivu provinces. Zaire accuses Tutsi-led Rwanda of fomenting the revolt and invading, a charge Rwanda denies.
Hutus from Burundi, which like Rwanda has been plagued by Tutsi-Hutu rivalry for generations, have also fled the area along with several hundred thousand Zaireans.
